name: Yaesu FT-277R
notes: 70 cm sibling of the FT-270R: same chassis, keypad, menu tree and clone protocol, different RF deck. Figures come from the Chicago-Offline ft270-277-info repo (SPECS.md, PROGRAMMING-TOOLS.md) and from CHIRP's VX-177 driver, which is the transport: the FT-277R is the amateur-branded sibling of the Vertex VX-177, and chirp/drivers/vx170.py VX177Radio subclasses VX170Radio, changing only the model ID ('AH022U') and valid_bands. All channel-storage limits are therefore inherited from the VX-170: memory_bounds (1, 200) and char name[6] display names. modes is ["FM"] (driver MODES ["FM", "NFM"], no AM) and bandwidths_khz 12.5/25 follows that split. The TX band is the US amateur 70 cm allocation 430-450 MHz; the wider 420-470 MHz span is the driver's valid_bands and is marked rx_only because stock firmware will not transmit outside the ham band and no MARS/CAP procedure has been verified. Note this rules out GMRS/FRS (462-467 MHz) on a stock radio even though the receiver tunes there. max_zones is 1 as a profile-0.1 compatibility shim; the driver sets has_bank = False. NOT HARDWARE VERIFIED: the driver hard-checks the clone image model ID, so a stock CHIRP may reject an FT-277R image; the pending CHIRP patch adds the real model string. Never write a VX-170/FT-270R image into this radio — VHF band data in a 70 cm PA is at best useless.
